name: Question 16
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4}+4t\,,\,{t}^{3}-2t\,,\,2{t}^{3}-3t⟩,$ find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}+4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3}+4,\,3{t}^{2}-2,\,6{t}^{2}-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c\,⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c\,⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩ \\ ⟨4{t}^{3}+4,\,3{t}^{2}-2,\,6{t}^{2}-3⟩ & =c\,⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩ \\ ⟨4{t}^{3}+4,\,3{t}^{2}-2,\,6{t}^{2}-3⟩ & =⟨0\,,\,c\,,\,3c⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{t}^{3}+4=0 \\ 3{t}^{2}-2=c \\ 6{t}^{2}-3=3c\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain that $t=-1.$ Substituting to the second equation, we get $c=1.$
These values also satisfy the third equation. 

Therefore, $⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=-1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨(-1)^{4}+4(-1)\,,\,(-1)^{3}-2(-1)\,,\,2(-1)^{3}-3(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,1,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(-3,1,1).$

Question 16
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨t4+4t,t3−2t,2t3−3t⟩, find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector ⟨0,1,3⟩.

a
(−3,1,1)
b
 (5,−1,−1) and (−3,1,1)
c
 (5,−1,−1)
d
 (0,0,0) and (−3,1,1)
e
 (24,4,10)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=⟨ddt(t4+4t),ddt(t3−2t),ddt(2t3−3t)⟩=⟨4t3+4,3t2−2,6t2−3⟩

The vectors r′(t) and ⟨0,1,3⟩ are parallel for some specific value t0 of the parameter t if and only if there exists a constant c such that r′(t0)=c⟨0,1,3⟩. So, we have

r′(t)=c⟨0,1,3⟩⟨4t3+4,3t2−2,6t2−3⟩=c⟨0,1,3⟩⟨4t3+4,3t2−2,6t2−3⟩=⟨0,c,3c⟩.

Equating the components gives:

{4t3+4=03t2−2=c6t2−3=3c

From the first equation, we obtain that t=−1. Substituting to the second equation, we get c=1. These values also satisfy the third equation.

Therefore, ⟨0,1,3⟩ and r′ are parallel only at the point corresponding to t=−1.

Finally, since r(−1)=⟨(−1)4+4(−1),(−1)3−2(−1),2(−1)3−3(−1)⟩=⟨−3,1,1⟩,

we conclude that ⟨0,1,3⟩ and r′(t) are parallel at the point (−3,1,1).
